title: What comes to pass is not outside the Doer
subtitle: Raag Gauree · Ang 154
summary: The shabad begins with the blunt fact that past actions cannot be erased. It moves through uncertainty about outcomes and ends in a harder peace: what pleases the Divine comes to pass, and there is no other Doer.
whyItMatters: This is for anyone who feels trapped in regret, replay, or bargaining with the past. Stayed with, it does not sentimentalize pain, but it loosens the argument with reality.
takeaway: Let this stay with you: regret quiets when the heart returns the moment to Hukam.

lines.translation: What do we know of what will happen hereafter?
Whatever pleases Him shall come to pass.
There is no other Doer except Him. ||1||

lines.gurmukhi: ਨਾ ਜਾਣਾ ਕਰਮ ਕੇਵਡ ਤੇਰੀ ਦਾਤਿ ॥
lines.transliteration: naa jaanaa karam kevadd teree dhaat ||
lines.translation: I do not know about karma, or how great Your gifts are.

lines.gurmukhi: ਕਰਮੁ ਧਰਮੁ ਤੇਰੇ ਨਾਮ ਕੀ ਜਾਤਿ ॥੧॥ ਰਹਾਉ ॥
lines.transliteration: karam dharam tere naam kee jaat ||1|| rahaau ||
lines.translation: The karma of actions, the Dharma of righteousness, social class and status, are contained within Your Name. ||1||Pause||
You are So Great, O Giver, O Great Giver!
The treasure of Your devotional worship is never exhausted.
One who takes pride in himself shall never be right.
The soul and body are all at Your disposal. ||2||
You kill and rejuvenate. You forgive and merge us into Yourself.
As it pleases You, You inspire us to chant Your Name.

lines.gurmukhi: ਤੂੰ ਦਾਨਾ ਬੀਨਾ ਸਾਚਾ ਸਿਰਿ ਮੇਰੈ ॥
lines.transliteration: too(n) dhaanaa beenaa saachaa sir merai ||
lines.translation: You are All-knowing, All-seeing and True, O my Supreme Lord.
Please, bless me with the Guru's Teachings; my faith is in You alone. ||3||

lines.gurmukhi: ਤਨ ਮਹਿ ਮੈਲੁ ਨਾਹੀ ਮਨੁ ਰਾਤਾ ॥
lines.transliteration: tan meh mail naahee man raataa ||
lines.translation: One whose mind is attuned to the Lord, has no pollution in his body.
Through the Guru's Word, the True Shabad is realized.
All Power is Yours, through the greatness of Your Name.
Nanak abides in the Sanctuary of Your devotees. ||4||10||

structure: First, it begins by refusing the fantasy that the past can be edited after the fact.
Then, it stays honest about how little the ego knows of what comes next.
Finally, it ends in the hard mercy that there is no other Doer outside the Divine will.
